scope: Automatic portrait blink, reduced-motion neutral restoration, bounded shared mesh and graphics context restoration

independentChecks.qualification: Fresh final source; three shared-head/blink plus four motion tests
Scheduling and listener accounting, not independent GPU rendering

independentChecks.check: Source/frozen copy and capture digest bindings

checks: Observed actual automatic fully closed pose before graphics fault
Reduced motion restores exact neutral PNG while GL is unavailable
Real WEBGL_lose_context fallback and exact same-canvas renderer restoration
One CPU mesh across selected poses/cameras; six movement projection agreements and unchanged selected player DTO

sourceObservations: Neutral href retained at mount so reopening does not depend on unavailable graphics; new closed poses use shared rendering/cache
Five quantized blink poses with explicit80ms plateau; quantization extends time spent at maximum beyond the plateau, so not measured physiology
Hidden/offscreen/reduced state cancels RAF and opens the portrait; visible phase resumes using elapsed active presentation time, no football RNG
Loss handler prevents default, disposes renderer, clears PNGs and retains canvas/CPU mesh; restore enables creation of fresh GPU resources
Cleanup removes observers, media/document listeners and RAF idempotently

findings.description: Open/closed distinction is readable in inspected real desktop/mobile portraits. Bulged folds, planar/mannequin facial forms, painted beard, simplified lips and neck material discontinuity remain; this functional restoration is not complete appearance acceptance.

Only explicit graphics-context-loss recovery is covered; unrelated shader/draw failures still choose session fallback. Broader devices, repeated loss/restore stress and all saved heads remain unverified.

limits: Four controlled-pose originals inspected; actual automatic-cycle success comes from hash-bound primary browser test, not screenshots alone
No built deployment/career/all-person or full-suite acceptance
No physiological blink calibration or demographic/anatomical fitting
Whole appearance and release remain open
